question.text: Will the Plymouth County DA's office announce before January 1, 2027 that it will retry Lindsay Clancy?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, before January 1, 2027, according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) the Plymouth County District Attorney's Office publicly announces it intends to retry Lindsay Clancy on any charges related to the 2023 [killings of the Clancy children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_the_Clancy_children).

research:
Checks are done; here is the summary. In short: on 2026-11-02 an assistant DA told the judge in open court that "this will be a retrial," but the office has not yet made a formal, unconditional announcement of what it plans to do.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question has no data series behind it. It resolves on credible reports that the Plymouth County DA's Office publicly announced it intends to retry Clancy. I couldn't fetch the background WCVB article (the site blocked my fetch). It reported on 2026-09-29 that DA Tim Cruz was still "working on" the decision.
- 2026-11-02: Assistant DA Jennifer Sprague said in open court: "Your honor, this would be a retrial. As to what that looks like will depend... We're not at that point yet." [USA TODAY via Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/prosecutors-intend-retry-lindsay-clancy-172408508.html); [AP via Just the News](https://justthenews.com/nation/crime/prosecutors-say-they-will-pursue-retrial-lindsay-clancy-are-still-working-out-details)

## 2. Current status
- The question may already be close to settled. On 2026-11-02, major outlets reported the courtroom statement as the office's intent to retry:
  - USA TODAY headline: "Prosecutors intend to retry Lindsay Clancy for killing her 3 children." [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/prosecutors-intend-retry-lindsay-clancy-172408508.html)
  - AP headline: "Prosecutors say they will pursue retrial for Lindsay Clancy but are still working out details." [Just the News](https://justthenews.com/nation/crime/prosecutors-say-they-will-pursue-retrial-lindsay-clancy-are-still-working-out-details)
- The caveats:
  - CBS Boston said Sprague signaled Clancy "will likely stand trial again." [CBS Boston](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/lindsay-clancy-hearing-new-second-trial/)
  - The AP version phrased it conditionally: prosecutors plan to retry "if the case proceeds." [NBC CT/AP](https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/local/lindsay-clancy-trial-retried-judge-hears-motions/3791497/)
  - HNGN called it "the clearest sign yet" but "not formal." It reported that Cruz said his office is still reviewing and expects to say more after Nov. 16. [HNGN](https://www.hngn.com/articles/273677/20261103/judge-eyes-march-retrial-lindsay-clancy-charges-undecided.htm)
  - Charges are undecided: first-degree murder, second-degree murder, or something lesser.
- Whether the question resolves Yes now depends on whether a line-prosecutor statement in court counts as the office "publicly announcing." I found no news release or press statement from Cruz himself.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Judge William Sullivan said March 2027 is "probably realistic" for a retrial but won't set a date until he rules on the motions. He took three motions under advisement: the defense's double-jeopardy motion to dismiss, the prosecution's gag-order request, and the request for the holdout juror's records. [HNGN](https://www.hngn.com/articles/273677/20261103/judge-eyes-march-retrial-lindsay-clancy-charges-undecided.htm)
- 2026-11-02: Prosecutors said they won't decide the charges until Sullivan rules on the motions. One report adds that the office may wait for any appeals of those rulings. [USA TODAY/Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/prosecutors-intend-retry-lindsay-clancy-172408508.html); [CBS Boston](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/lindsay-clancy-hearing-new-second-trial/)
- 2026-11-02: Defense lawyer Kevin Reddington asked for a spring trial, before Sullivan retires, and has said he'd accept a plea deal that avoids prison. Martin Weinberg, also for the defense, argued that a retrial would violate double jeopardy. [AP/Just the News](https://justthenews.com/nation/crime/prosecutors-say-they-will-pursue-retrial-lindsay-clancy-are-still-working-out-details)
- 2026-09-29: Cruz said he was still "working on" the retrial decision. [WCVB](https://www.wcvb.com/article/lindsay-clancy-tim-cruz-retrial-decision-question-sept-29/73943192)
- 2026-09-04: Mistrial declared after seven days of jury deliberations and a deadlock. Cruz said he would decide later. [Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/09/04/metro/da-cruz-retry-lindsay-clancy/); [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/04/us/live-news/lindsay-clancy-trial)

## 4. Base rates
- I found no formal statistics. US prosecutors usually retry high-profile murder cases after a hung jury, especially when, as here, the jury reportedly split 11-1 (per Manifold's AI-generated summary, unverified). Plea deals are the main alternative.
- On 2026-09-04, former Florida prosecutor Dave Aronberg told CNN a plea deal was more likely than a retrial. [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/04/us/live-news/lindsay-clancy-trial)
- The two-month gap between the mistrial and the Nov. 2 courtroom statement shows how slowly this office moves before committing.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Manifold, "Will Lindsay Clancy stand trial again": 70%. It closes in 2029 and needs a sworn jury, a stricter bar than this question's "announces intent." [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/JimD/will-lindsay-clancy-stand-trial-aga)

  - Convicted of manslaughter in 2026: 3.4%.

  - These say little about an announcement. The low 2026 figures mainly reflect a 2027 trial date.
- Kalshi: none of the collected markets matches. The "most-searched person" market showing Clancy at 34% is unrelated.
- I found no market on this exact question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-16: Status hearing. Sullivan is expected to rule on the motion to dismiss and, if he denies it, set a retrial date, possibly in March 2027. Cruz has said he will say more after this date. [HNGN](https://www.hngn.com/articles/273677/20261103/judge-eyes-march-retrial-lindsay-clancy-charges-undecided.htm); [CBS Boston](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/lindsay-clancy-hearing-new-second-trial/)
- Ways the Nov. 16 outcome could cut:
  - If the case is dismissed on double jeopardy grounds, the DA would likely appeal rather than announce a retrial.
  - A plea deal or a decision to reduce charges is still possible; Reddington is open to a deal.
  - If prosecutors pursue second-degree murder, Clancy could choose a trial by judge instead of a jury.
- Pending rulings on the gag order and juror records could also shape what the DA's office says publicly.

## 1. Resolution source

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time and what has to happen.** There are about 8 weeks left, until January 1, 2027. Yes requires credible reports that the Plymouth County DA's Office publicly announced it intends to retry Clancy on any related charge.

**(b) Status quo.** On 2026-11-02, Assistant DA Jennifer Sprague told the court "this would be a retrial." AP and USA TODAY headlined this as prosecutors intending to retry Clancy. Their wording was "say they will pursue retrial" and "intend to retry." A resolver may well count this already. The question text says the criteria were not yet satisfied, but that may predate November 2. The office has issued no formal statement from DA Tim Cruz himself, and Cruz says he will say more after the November 16 hearing.

**(c) Base rate.** In high-profile US murder cases that end in a hung jury, especially one reportedly split 11-1 toward conviction, prosecutors retry or announce a retrial roughly 70-85% of the time. Plea deals and dropped charges make up the rest.

**(d) Evidence.**
- For Yes:
  - 2026-11-02: open-court statement that "this would be a retrial."
  - 2026-11-02: AP and USA TODAY headlines framed it as intent to retry.
  - 2026-11-03: the judge said a March 2027 trial is "probably realistic."
  - Cruz said he would say more after November 16.
- For No:
  - 2026-11-02: the statement was hedged ("we're not at that point yet") and charges are undecided.
  - CBS said Clancy "will likely" stand trial again, and AP added "if the case proceeds."
  - A double-jeopardy motion to dismiss is pending.
  - The defense is open to a plea deal.
  - The office has moved slowly since the September 4 mistrial.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: The judge grants the double-jeopardy dismissal (unlikely, since a hung jury normally permits retrial). The DA appeals, and the resolver judges the November 2 courtroom remark too informal to count. Alternatively, the parties negotiate a plea instead.
- Yes: The judge denies the motion on November 16 and sets a March trial. Cruz then announces the charges for the retrial, or the resolver simply credits the November 2 statement that the press widely reported as intent to retry.

**(f) From base rate to forecast.** I start from a base rate of about 75%. I move up because there is already an on-record courtroom statement reported as intent to retry, and a scheduled point (after November 16) at which Cruz expects to clarify. I hold back from the extremes for three reasons: the risk of dismissal on double-jeopardy grounds, the chance of a plea deal, and ambiguity over whether a line prosecutor's remark counts as the office announcing.

Probability: 87%

(a) About 8 weeks remain, until January 1, 2027. Yes requires credible reports that the Plymouth County DA's Office publicly announced it intends to retry Lindsay Clancy on any related charges.

(b) Status quo: on 2026-11-02, Assistant DA Jennifer Sprague told the court "this would be a retrial." AP and USA Today headlines framed this as prosecutors intending to retry. This may already satisfy the criteria. However, the question text says the criteria are not yet met, and the office says it is still working out the details. Without a further step, resolution depends on how the Nov 2 statement is judged.

(c) Base rate: after hung juries in high-profile US murder cases, especially with a lopsided split, prosecutors announce a retrial roughly 65-75% of the time. Most of the rest end in plea deals or dismissals. Announcements usually come within a few months.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - The Nov 2 in-court statement, "this would be a retrial."
  - Headlines from AP, USA Today and Yahoo saying prosecutors intend or will pursue a retrial.
  - The judge said March 2027 is "probably realistic."
  - Cruz said he would say more after the Nov 16 hearing.
- For No:
  - On Sept 29, Cruz was still "working on" the decision.
  - AP phrased it conditionally ("if the case proceeds"), and HNGN called it "not formal."
  - The charges are undecided, and the office may wait for appeals of the judge's rulings.
  - The defense is open to a non-prison plea.
